course.tagline: Sell with confidence: find buyers, handle objections and close the deal.

days.challenge: Explain selling to a friend in 30 seconds, without using the word sell.
days.goal: Explain what selling really is: helping someone solve a problem.

options: Helping someone solve a problem with a product they need

options: Good sellers listen first, understand, then offer the right fix

video.title: LIVE Sales Training - Blocking Objections

Read it word for word always

Add your three best questions from day 6.

video.title: 4-Step Selling Formula: Win Hearts, Close Deals

days.challenge: Listen to a friend talk for two minutes without interrupting once.
days.goal: Listen well and find the buyer's real need.

quiz.explain: Listening means giving full attention, not thinking about what to say next.
options: Giving full attention, not planning your next words
Nodding while thinking of your pitch
quiz.q: What does real listening mean?

quiz.explain: Buyers tell you their real need when they feel heard, not rushed.
options: Buyers tell you when they feel heard
Buyers want you to talk more
quiz.q: Why listen before you pitch?

options: Repeating back shows you understood and builds trust
quiz.q: Why repeat back what the buyer said?

steps: In your next talk, listen for two full minutes without interrupting.
Note the exact words the buyer uses about their problem.
Repeat back the main point in your own words.
Ask: did I get that right?
Write down the real need you heard.

days.challenge: Rewrite your product pitch using only benefits, no features.
days.goal: Show benefits, not features.

quiz.explain: A feature is what a product has. A benefit is how it helps the buyer.
options: A feature is what it has, a benefit is how it helps
quiz.q: What is the difference between a feature and a benefit?

quiz.explain: Buyers care about what the product does for them, not its technical details.
options: Buyers care about what it does for them
quiz.q: Why do benefits sell better than features?

options: Ask: so what does that mean for the buyer?

steps: List five features of your product.
For each one, write the benefit: what it means for the buyer.
Cross out the features from your pitch.
Rewrite your pitch using only benefits.
Practise the new pitch out loud.
Use it with a real prospect today.
days.task: Rewrite your pitch using only benefits, and use it with a real prospect.

video.title: The Marketing Funnel Explained: What Is It & How To Write One

days.challenge: Answer the price question in three different ways and pick the best.
days.goal: Handle the price question with confidence.

quiz.explain: When buyers ask about price, they often mean: is it worth it?
options: They often mean: is it worth it?
They are ready to buy at once
quiz.q: What does it's too expensive usually mean?

quiz.explain: Show the value first, then the price, so the buyer sees what they get.
options: Show the value first, then the price

options: Break it into a daily or weekly cost

steps: Write down your price and what the buyer gets for it.
Write three ways to explain the value before the price.
Practise saying the price calmly, without rushing.

options: Ask what they need to think about

options: Agree a clear next step and a time to talk again

Write three gentle replies that ask what they need to think about.

Agree a clear next step: a call or message on a set day.

days.task: Write three replies to I need to think about it and use the best one.
